title: Chapter 297: Are You a Ghost?
html:
Chen Ge ended the call and gripped the doorknob. His right hand closed around the hammer while his left eased the door open a crack. Light spilled into the corridor, the thin wooden door seeming to divide two different worlds.

“Who are you looking for?”

A tall, gaunt man stood outside. His eyes were sunken, his skin rough, and exhaustion hung over him.

“I came to give you a warning.” The man kept a fair distance from the door. “Don’t stay here overnight. If you have to stay within this residential area, do not stay on this floor.”

“Why?” Chen Ge wanted to hear what this strange man had to say.

“The reason doesn’t matter. Just don’t spend the night.” He coughed twice and covered his mouth with the hand from his right pocket, as if afraid of being overheard. “Someone disappeared on this floor,” he whispered.

“Disappeared?” Chen Ge recalled the agency’s records. Room 304’s second tenant, an English teacher, had vanished inside the apartment.

“Leave while you still can.” The man appeared like he had come to warn Chen Ge out of kindness.

“How do you know all this? Do you live here?” Chen Ge leaned halfway through the opening, keeping his hammer concealed behind the door.

“Yes, upstairs. Earlier, I overheard you talking to yourself.” Dust covered the man’s jacket, and both hands remained buried in its pockets. He looked frail and swayed unsteadily. “I expected you to leave, but instead you rushed into the apartment. When I realized you meant to stay overnight, I came to warn you.”

“Talking to myself?” Chen Ge swallowed. Most people would already have begun to panic. “Has this happened to other visitors?”

“Yes, but normally people come during broad daylight. This is the first time someone has visited at night.”

“What happened to those people?”

“Some lost their minds; others became tenants. Those who went mad were the fortunate ones. Everyone who actually moved in either committed suicide or disappeared.”

“Went mad? Disappeared? Why are the endings so different?”

“There seems to be a reason.” The man beckoned with his right hand, but Chen Ge refused to approach, forcing him to lean closer instead. “I heard that the people who went mad found the property through a real agent. Those who became tenants called the ghost agent’s number.”

“Ghost agent?” Chen Ge was reminded of the girl’s voice who remained the same throughout their conversation, the only defining feature about her voice being the politeness. “What is a ghost agent?”

“It began several years ago, when a real-estate agent was murdered in Room 304 next door. The killer has never been caught.” The man drew a deep breath and looked upstairs. Beyond the light from Chen Ge’s apartment, darkness smothered every corner, making it impossible to tell what had caught his attention.

After surveying the corridor, he continued. “The apartment has remained vacant since his death, yet strange things keep happening. Prospective tenants arrive from time to time, but each gives a different explanation for finding the listing. Some saw it online, others on roadside advertisements, and a few cannot remember how the information entered their minds at all.”

The man paused while he looked at Chen Ge with confusion. “By the way, how did you find out about this place? And… how did you get the key to the room next to Room 304?”

“It’s complicated.” Chen Ge glanced toward Room 304. “I called the number posted on its door. Then a man around thirty, dressed in a black shirt, arrived and gave me this key.”

“Around thirty? A black shirt?” the man muttered. His eyes widened. “He’s back!”

After saying that, the man rushed upstairs like he was running for his life.

“Wait! Finish the story!” The man was too suspicious to let escape. Chen Ge seized his hammer and pursued him. Whether or not the fugitive saw the weapon, he sprinted desperately upstairs. The old building had only eight floors. By the time they reached the fifth, Chen Ge’s phone began ringing.

“Stop!” Chen Ge did not allow himself to get distracted. He rushed until the sixth floor when he finally caught up to the thin man. “Why did you run?”

“The agent was in his thirties! When he died, blood soaked his white dress shirt until it looked black!” Panic distorted the man’s face, and Chen Ge’s fearsome hammer did nothing to reassure him.

Just as I suspected. The agent I met must have been the first tenant. The question is whether the woman on the phone is also a ghost.His phone continued ringing. As Chen Ge took it out, the gaunt man pressed against the railing to remain as far away as possible.

The screen displayed the records sent by customer service. The first image described the third tenant—the gambler—and thoughtfully included his photograph at the bottom.

“Gaunt, exhausted, with sunken eyes!” Chen Ge’s body reacted before conscious thought. He raised the hammer and swung toward the railing. He had suspected the truth from the moment they met: the man used only his right hand and never removed his left from his pocket. Chen Ge had wondered whether that arm existed at all.

The hammer crashed into the railing as the gaunt man twisted aside at an unnatural angle. He made no attempt to fight. Wearing a strange smile, he vaulted over the railing and dropped toward the third floor.

He’s probably run back to Room 304.

Chen Ge had left the recorder behind. To prevent any further surprises, he returned to the third floor. Once safely inside Room 305, he switched it on.

This building is fascinating. Everyone sounds truthful, yet everyone lies. I can trust no one.Chen Ge reconsidered the gaunt man’s warning. Why was the gambler so determined to make me leave?

After picking up all his stuff, Chen Ge took out his phone and looked at the screen.

Customer service sent information about the gambler but not the other two tenants. Was that deliberate? How are these people connected to the drawer?Chen Ge shook his head. The Baleful Specter I drew this time is certainly unusual.

He called the agent’s number. He held the hammer in one hand, and his other held his phone to his ear.

“Good evening. The information has been sent to your phone. How may I help you?” The woman remained unfailingly polite despite the approaching midnight hour.

“Yes, I still have one last question to ask.”

“Please, go ahead.”

“I’m sorry, but are you a ghost?”
